scenes.visual: close-up illustration of a shiny steel Indian pressure cooker on a gas stove, its heavy round whistle weight on the lid glowing bright red-orange and lifting slightly with a big white puff of steam bursting out from under it, blue gas flame below, deep teal kitchen wall background, the cooker large and filling the lower two-thirds of the frame, no people, no text or logos
scenes.narration: Your cooker whistles almost every day. But what's that sound *actually* telling you?

scenes.visual: 2D animation: an open pot on a flame, steam floating away, the temperature number climbs to 100 and sticks
scenes.narration: Yesterday's odd one out? B. Not *done*. It's saying something stranger. In an open pot, water gets stuck at a *hundred* degrees.
scenes.headline: STUCK AT *100*

scenes.visual: illustration of a hand turning the knob of a gas stove up, under an open steel pot of boiling water with big white clouds of steam rising out of the top and drifting away, the blue-orange flame bright and big, plain navy background, the pot and hand large in the lower two-thirds of the frame, no text
scenes.narration: Turn the flame up, it still won't climb. Extra heat just makes *steam*, and the steam floats away. So... what if it can't?
scenes.headline: STEP 1/3: *STEAM* LEAVES

scenes.visual: illustration of two hands pressing down and twisting the lid of a steel pressure cooker shut, the rubber ring at the lid edge glowing bright red-orange, white steam curling inside a clean cutaway window in the cooker side, plain deep teal background, the cooker large and close in the lower two-thirds of the frame, no text
scenes.narration: Now here's the trick. Lock the lid, and the steam's *trapped*. Like a packed room with one heavy door. Everyone pushes, even down on the water.
scenes.headline: STEP 2/3: *TRAPPED*

scenes.visual: 2D animation: lid goes on, trapped steam crowds in, arrows press on the water, the temperature climbs 100 to 121
scenes.narration: And pressed-down water needs *more* heat to boil. A hundred and ten... a hundred and *twenty*. Hotter than boiling.
scenes.headline: HOTTER THAN *BOILING*

scenes.visual: close-up side cutaway illustration of the top of a steel pressure cooker lid, a thin metal vent pipe rising from the lid with a heavy round whistle weight sitting on top of it, the weight bright red-orange, the inside of the pipe shown in a clean cutaway, plain navy background, the weight and pipe large and centred in the lower two-thirds of the frame, no text
scenes.narration: So why doesn't it burst? See that weight on top? It sits on one tiny pipe. That's the heavy *door*.
scenes.headline: STEP 3/3: THE *DOOR*

scenes.visual: 2D animation: the weight on the vent pipe, a PUSH bar fills, the weight lifts, steam bursts out, WHISTLE, the weight drops back
scenes.narration: <short pause> When the push gets strong *enough*, it lifts the door. Steam rushes out... that's your whistle. Then it drops and shuts again.
scenes.headline: THAT'S THE *WHISTLE*

scenes.visual: warm illustration of a smiling young Indian woman in a simple home kitchen lifting a steaming bowl of yellow dal next to a steel pressure cooker on the stove, the bowl of dal the brightest thing in the frame in sunny yellow-orange, soft cool blue-grey kitchen background, the woman and bowl large in the lower two-thirds of the frame, no text
scenes.narration: So it's not a timer. It's letting off *pressure*. And that extra heat is why your dal cooks so fast. Next time it whistles, you'll know.
scenes.headline: NOT A *TIMER*

scenes.headline: *SHOUTOUT*

youtube.title: Why a pressure cooker whistle means it's past 100°C #shorts
youtube.description:
Why does a pressure cooker whistle? Not because the food is done. In an open pot, water gets stuck at 100°C: extra heat just turns it into steam that floats away. Lock the cooker's lid and the steam is trapped, pressing down on the water, so the water has to get hotter before it can boil, about 120°C. The heavy weight on the lid sits on a tiny vent pipe. When the pressure pushes hard enough, it lifts the weight, steam rushes out (that's the pressure cooker whistle), and the weight drops back to seal it again. That extra heat is how a pressure cooker works so fast.
